name: LinkedIn Newsroom
tagline: Breaking AI news to an approved LinkedIn post, from my phone

nodes.label: n8n tick
nodes.body: n8n starts one run at a time. A stuck run's lock expires after 90 minutes, and a health check restarts n8n if it jams or goes quiet for 25 minutes.

nodes.label: 57 sources
nodes.body: Lab newsrooms and sitemaps, the White House and UK PM, OpenAI and Claude status pages, SDK releases, OpenRouter, Hugging Face, Techmeme, Bloomberg, CNBC, Hacker News, Reddit, Bluesky, lab YouTube channels, leak trackers and Google News for the last hour.

nodes.label: Fresh filter
nodes.body: Anything seen before is skipped. Stories older than 12 hours are dropped before any model sees them.

nodes.label: Jev rates
nodes.body: TypeSafe's Jev model answers four typed questions per story: impact, interest from 1 to 10, is it a launch, and is it a duplicate of anything covered in the last 3 days. Twelve stories take under a second.

fallback.log: Jev is offline. Claude Haiku takes over and rates the run

nodes.label: Haiku backup
nodes.body: If Jev errors, Claude Haiku rates that run on the same scale. If credit runs out, Jev pauses for an hour and comes back by itself.

nodes.label: Fixed rules
nodes.body: Duplicates become noise. Rumours and stories over 6 hours old are capped at 7. When two outlets cover one event in a run, the better rated one stays.

nodes.label: Dropped
nodes.body: Most stories end here. Being early only matters for the few that deserve a post.

nodes.label: Nightly digest
nodes.body: Second tier stories wait for a nightly carousel instead of a post of their own.

nodes.label: Daily budget
nodes.body: At most six drafts a day, so the feed never turns into spam.

nodes.label: Breaking alert
nodes.body: Over the limit, a strong story still reaches my phone as a Breaking AI news alert with the source link.

nodes.label: Opus drafts
nodes.body: Claude Opus finds the first publication time, verifies every number and quote, then writes a time line, the stakes, a labelled take, the strongest counter and a two sided question.

nodes.label: Checker
nodes.body: Sends a draft back once for dashes, length, hashtag count, a missing take or question, bait phrases, or photos without a free licence.

nodes.label: Card render
nodes.body: Builds the 4:5 card: an HD still for people posters, a seamless looping GIF where motion helps, a PNG otherwise.

nodes.label: My approval
nodes.body: Every draft arrives as one phone notification with Approve, Edit on Mac and Reject. Nothing posts without my tap.

nodes.label: LinkedIn
nodes.body: Posted through the LinkedIn API with companies tagged. The Posted notice lists people to tag by hand and reminds me to reply in the first hour.

name: First to Apply
tagline: New job postings screened, priced and on my phone within minutes

nodes.label: n8n tick
nodes.body: Five steps run in order. Each writes its result to disk, so a failure is visible instead of silent, and one lock per step means runs never overlap.

nodes.label: 214 career pages
nodes.body: Greenhouse, Lever, Ashby, SmartRecruiters, Workable and Recruitee publish a job the moment a company posts it, the earliest signal there is. Job board alerts arrive a day later at best.

nodes.label: Jev screens
nodes.body: Jev reads the posting against my profile and answers seven typed questions: role family, seniority, eligible from India, fit from 1 to 10, hard blockers, stated pay against my band, and whether hidden text is trying to steer AI screeners.

nodes.label: Dropped
nodes.body: Every dropped job keeps its reason, so the screen can be audited and tuned.

nodes.label: Claude prices
nodes.body: Claude estimates total pay at the level I would likely get, using company tiers, then writes one line on why I fit and one on the biggest risk.

fallback.log: Claude is offline. Jobs publish with Jev's verdict, pay marked not estimated yet

nodes.label: Priority rules
nodes.body: Fixed rules, so the tracker never disagrees with itself. P1: strong fit, in band, top tier company. P2: strong fit with a level gap or unknown pay. P3: kept as interview practice.

nodes.label: Tracker sheet
nodes.body: Every kept job lands in the tracker with its priority, fit, pay band and risk line.

nodes.label: Phone push
nodes.body: Only P1 and P2 roles posted in the last 48 hours buzz my phone. A company's first check lands quietly.

nodes.label: My tap
nodes.body: I decide. The pipeline drafts everything, but applying stays a human tap.

nodes.label: Referral ask
nodes.body: P1 roles ask for a referral first: contact searches, a drafted note, and a one tap email draft. The application waits 48 hours for it.

nodes.label: Applied
nodes.body: Referred or not, the application goes in. The follow up turns amber after 4 days.

name: Inbox Triage
tagline: Every email labelled, and my phone buzzes only for the few that need me

nodes.label: Gmail
nodes.body: New mail is picked up within a minute by Apps Script on Google, so it keeps working when my laptop is closed.

nodes.label: Sheet rules
nodes.body: Rules, clients, people, my businesses and learned senders live in a Sheet. Login codes, job alerts and known bulk senders are settled here without any model.

nodes.label: Jev classifies
nodes.body: Jev classifies whatever the rules could not settle against the label descriptions in the Sheet, and says how sure it is. Rewriting a description changes how mail is sorted.

nodes.label: Claude decides
nodes.sub: on my Mac, unsure ones only
nodes.body: Every 15 minutes Claude takes only what Jev was unsure about, picks a label or creates a new one (at most 3 a day, each with an Undo button), then remembers the sender.

fallback.log: The Mac is asleep. After 30 minutes the email alerts as possibly important

nodes.label: Unsure alert
nodes.body: If the Mac is asleep, an unsure email from a real person still alerts after 30 minutes as possibly important, so a sleeping laptop never hides a human.

nodes.label: Gmail label
nodes.body: The label is applied in Gmail. Nothing is ever archived, deleted or marked read.

nodes.label: Silent labels
nodes.body: Most mail lands quietly in its label: bank, payments, dev notifications, newsletters and promotions.

nodes.label: 11:00 briefing
nodes.body: One morning briefing: counts per label, threads waiting for a reply, what Claude is still deciding, and health. Senders and subjects only, never email bodies.

nodes.label: Phone alert
nodes.body: Only clients, customers of my products, replies from companies I applied to and real people buzz the phone. Overnight only the urgent ones ring.

nodes.label: My tap
nodes.body: Every alert has Open, Not important, Mute sender and Mark client. Each tap teaches the sorter.

nodes.label: Learns the sender
nodes.body: Taps and replies become rules in the Sheet, so the next email from that sender is settled before any model runs.

name: Claude Watchdog
tagline: Keeps watch over every Claude Code chat on my Mac and taps me only when one needs me

nodes.label: Minute scan
nodes.body: A LaunchAgent runs one scan a minute across every Claude Code chat on this Mac: the chats themselves, their workflows, background agents and background shells.

nodes.label: Hook notes
nodes.body: Four Claude Code hooks leave a note for the next scan: every finished turn, every API failure, every permission prompt or question, and every chat that closes.

nodes.label: Self check
nodes.body: A watcher that dies quietly is worse than none. If no scan has run for 10 minutes, the next finished turn sends an alert that the watchdog is not scanning, with the command that starts it again.

nodes.label: Trouble finder
nodes.body: Spots chats waiting on me, chats stopped by an API error or a usage limit, stalled or failed workflows, silent background agents and shells, chats busy for a long time with no output, and questions left unanswered. Dev servers and deliberate waits are left alone.

nodes.label: Done notes
nodes.body: Long work that finishes, a turn, a workflow, an agent or a background task over 10 minutes, gets a short Done note with the chat's own summary, so I never sit waiting on something already finished.

nodes.label: Risk filter
nodes.body: A stuck background task that touches git, ssh, a push or a deploy skips the nudge and comes straight to me. A machine never decides those.

nodes.label: Haiku nudge
nodes.sub: only if the chat is idle
nodes.body: If the chat that owns the problem is idle, a throwaway Claude Haiku that can only send one message nudges it first, at most twice, 10 minutes apart. The nudge never asks a chat to commit, push, deploy, stop or rerun anything.

fallback.log: Haiku could not deliver the nudge, so the alert goes to my phone at once

nodes.label: Owning chat
nodes.body: The chat that started the work has the context, so it gets the first chance to fix it. A chat in the middle of a turn is never interrupted.

nodes.label: Phone alert
nodes.body: Then my phone and my Mac get one alert: what is stuck, for how long, whether a nudge was tried, and numbered steps to fix it.

nodes.label: My call
nodes.body: I decide what happens next. The watchdog never touches the work itself.

nodes.label: VS Code
nodes.body: VS Code comes to the front only after a minute without keyboard or mouse input, so it never steals keystrokes meant for another window.

nodes.label: Snooze
nodes.body: When a wait is expected, one command on the Mac snoozes that item for a set time, or for good. Every nudge tells the chat how to snooze it too.

nodes.label: One reminder
nodes.body: If I do nothing, one reminder follows 30 minutes later. Then it stays quiet, so it never turns into noise.

name: Self-Improving Trading Lab
tagline: A paper money research lab that improves itself and is built to make fooling itself hard
note: Paper money only. The daily runner is built and passed its dry run; stages marked planned come next. Most ideas fail, and nothing here promises returns.

stats.label: months on paper before a change

nodes.label: Daily run
nodes.body: n8n checks every 30 minutes and starts the day's research from 7 pm, or at the first wake after a missed evening. A run that fails names the failed step on my phone and tries once more; after two failures it waits for tomorrow.

nodes.label: Heads up
nodes.body: Built today: a start notice that says what will be tested. Planned: ten minutes before a run my phone asks first, with Delay 1 hour, Start now and Skip today. A delay says research resumes in an hour, then asks again.

nodes.label: Safe compute
nodes.body: Planned: heavy tests run only on charger power, use every core but two at low priority, ease off when macOS reports heat pressure, and keep the Mac awake only while the run lasts. Built today: every run measures its own time, CPU time and peak memory.

nodes.label: Research atlas
nodes.body: Memory comes first. The atlas records every idea, paper, study and finding with its outcome, and the trial log refuses a retuned copy of an old idea before it counts. Planned: a knowledge base rebuilt every run and handed to Claude, where each pattern carries a confidence label: spotted, promising, confirmed or proven live. Only a proven live pattern may change the strategy, and the knowledge base never carries sealed numbers.

nodes.label: Paper scout
nodes.body: Claude searches the web for newly published papers. Their text is treated as untrusted data: checked against a strict schema, stripped to plain text, and shown to the idea writer only inside a fenced data block. Each paper's claim is tested once on Indian data, so it ends up replicated or refuted.

nodes.label: Claude proposes
nodes.body: Claude reads the atlas and the new papers with every tool switched off, then proposes a few ideas, each with its economic reason and the direction it expects written down before any test. It never sees stock names or any result after the seal, and it never grades its own ideas.

fallback.log: Claude is unavailable, so the run stops here and nothing is counted. My phone hears which step failed, and it tries again once, 30 minutes later

nodes.label: Strategy menu
nodes.body: Ideas come from fixed menus across six kinds: stock factors; market timing from the rupee, the dollar, crude oil, bond yields and fear gauges; sector rotation; calendar windows around Union Budgets, RBI policy days, elections, festivals and F&O expiry; risk overlays; and position sizing, including a satellite of riskier bets capped at a fifth of the money. Planned: an adaptive weights family, where the rule that changes factor weights is the idea under test, never weights tuned by hand.

nodes.label: Trial register
nodes.body: Every idea is registered and counted before it is tested, so a failure still counts against the lab and raises the bar for every later result. At most 4 counted ideas a weekday, 20 a week and 500 a year. Descriptive studies are labelled as such and are never counted or promoted.

nodes.label: Fair test
nodes.body: Each idea is tested on frozen history from before the seal, with purged cross validation, and judged by a score that is discounted for every trial run so far. It also runs as a buy-only portfolio a person could hold, after costs, against the benchmark on the same days, and only an idea that beats the benchmark can ever be promoted. Planned: discovery on the older years, 1995 to 2014, and confirmation on 2015 up to the seal.

nodes.label: Failed ideas
nodes.body: Most ideas fail. Each failure stays in the atlas with the test it missed, so it is never tried again, and it will appear on the research page with the rest of the findings.

nodes.label: Cheat checks
nodes.body: A result that looks too good to be true is held for a manual audit. Once a month a deliberately leaky idea runs through every check and must be caught, or the lab switches itself off. Planned: placebo dates and random markets, where a real edge must vanish, plus bootstraps and cost scenarios.

nodes.label: Audit hold
nodes.body: A result that looks too good to be true stops that idea for a manual audit instead of moving on. In research that is almost always a bug or a leak, not a discovery. If the monthly leaky idea ever slips through, the whole lab stops itself.

nodes.label: Sealed period
nodes.body: Everything after 2 October 2026 is sealed. Only the promotion rules may query it, in the cloud, and they get back pass or fail with no numbers. Sealed data never reaches the laptop. The sealed tests start to mean something from about October 2027, as the period fills.

nodes.label: History ladder
nodes.body: Planned: before anything may change the live strategy it climbs a long history ladder: about 30 years of Indian stocks, the Sensex since 1979 for timing rules, Indian factor data from IIM Ahmedabad, US data back to 1926 and emerging markets since 1990. Each rung must show the idea's mechanism holds; on Indian data it must beat the current strategy on return and on worst loss, after costs. Built today: at least three months in the paper tier before a candidate is put to me.

nodes.label: Phone updates
nodes.body: A start notice, then a finish notice: how long the run took, CPU time, peak memory, what was tried and found, papers replicated or refuted, the trials used this week, and the new research version against the previous one. A failed run names the step that failed. Planned: an announcement for every change to a strategy or to the lab's own workflow.

nodes.label: Weekly round
nodes.body: Planned: once a week a deeper Claude round works on the lab itself: its tests, its menus, its own workflow, anything outside the locked rulebook. Each round must advance at least one idea from my own ideas inbox and log its reasoning, and it keeps an innovation radar that files new papers, code and models as watch, trial, adopt or reject.

nodes.label: Auditor agent
nodes.body: Planned: a separate auditor agent reviews every change the AI makes to the lab before it ships. The proposer never approves its own work, and nothing ships without the audit.

nodes.label: Locked rulebook
nodes.body: Built today: the trial log is create-only and the seal is enforced in code. Planned: the trial log, the seal, the gates, the caps and the promotion rules locked together and checked against a fingerprint on every run. Everything else the AI may improve, and every change is announced.

nodes.label: Exams
nodes.body: Planned: two standing exams of the lab's judgment. A weekly forecast tournament scores its probability calls for accuracy and calibration. A keep or sell exam runs thousands of realistic starting portfolios through history and grades which holdings it keeps and which it sells, after costs and tax.

nodes.label: Approval
nodes.body: A candidate reaches me only after it passed every research gate, the buy-only test and the sealed period, and spent at least three months in the paper tier. I tap Approve or Reject, and the first answer stands. An approval waits for the monthly review, so the live strategy changes at most once a month; the cloud step that applies it there is still being built. Planned: a candidate that also clears the history ladder goes live by itself, with 24 hours for me to undo it.

nodes.label: Paper engine
nodes.body: The live strategy trades paper money in the cloud every market day, on real prices with real costs. No real money is involved. A small AI filter reads company filings for red flags, and a flagged stock is left out. Planned: on trading days my phone hears only about exceptions.

nodes.label: Day checks
nodes.body: Planned: at 9:05, before the bell, only risk rules that have already been tested may act, and no new ideas. At 12:30 a risk-only check runs; the strategy itself never changes midday.

nodes.label: News desk
nodes.body: Planned: headlines and filings captured every 30 minutes from feeds the lab may legally use, each with its time and company. The AI filter scores each item when it arrives and the score is frozen, never rescored with hindsight. News shadow books compete forward from day one, and my phone hears about news only when it changes something.

nodes.label: Closing plan
nodes.body: Planned: at 15:45, after the close, the numbers rank the market and tomorrow's plan is written: a watch list with triggers set in advance, and news features over 1, 5 and 21 days for each stock. The live strategy applies only news rules that have passed the same tests.

nodes.label: Judgment desk
nodes.body: Planned: an AI judgment desk reads the day and makes its own calls, but only on a shadow portfolio. It earns any authority only if its record beats the rules going forward. Its judgment is never backtested, because the model already knows how history ended.

fallback.log: The desk is offline. The rules run the day alone, as they always do

nodes.label: Shadow books
nodes.body: Ideas that pass the research gates run as paper books in the cloud, scored against the live strategy on the same days from then on. Planned: the judgment desk and the news books join this contest, and nothing they do touches the live strategy until their record says so.

nodes.label: Findings
nodes.body: Every run writes at least one finding: a test result, a paper verdict, a study or a data note, with no stock names and no sealed numbers. Failures are kept with the rest, and they will be published when the research page launches.
